text: Git is a version control system that helps developers track changes in their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. For example, you can create a feature branch to build a new function safely. When your work is ready, you merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the project organised and reduces mistakes. By using feature branches, merging, and pull requests together, developers can collaborate smoothly and keep their code stable.
